body:
# Independent audit: intrinsic approximate cap covers

Auditor: `minkowski_transfer`. Verdict: **PASS**, with the nonclosed
Helly dependency made explicit below. Audited source:
`candidate 2623b39acd3d4a1d`,
Sections 1--9. No computation is needed for this finite convexity proof.

The exact conclusion is conditional: if at every positive intrinsic
fiber some at most t original caps leave residual q-measure at most
`ell(z)^q`, for a finite nonnegative convex threshold ell, then at most
kt original caps have that same pointwise residual bound on every
positive fiber. Here k counts occupied integer parities. This does not
establish that arbitrary critical cap families satisfy its premise.

## 1. Intrinsic measures and varying directions

There are finitely many nonempty integer fibers, each compact and
convex. Its Hausdorff dimension is its affine dimension. Consequently
q is an integer maximum, the q-dimensional fibers have finite positive
H_q, and all smaller-dimensional fibers have zero H_q. Finite Borel
additivity gives precisely `H_q(S)=sum V_z`, with no ambient volume or
Jacobian substituted. The standard H_q normalization is Euclidean
q-volume in each fiber's own affine plane.

The sets `U_J=C intersect intersection H_j^c` use the actual strict
complements of the closed caps. They are bounded Borel convex sets,
although not necessarily closed. Every nonempty convex section has
nonempty relative interior in its affine hull. Its H_q is positive and
finite when its affine dimension is q, and infinite when the affine
dimension exceeds q. Thus membership in a strict residual superlevel
forces a nonempty section of dimension at least q.

At two such endpoint sections, the proof correctly distinguishes all
possibilities. If either section has dimension greater than q, the
intermediate Minkowski combination has dimension greater than q. If
both have dimension q with distinct direction spaces, the dimension of
their sum is the dimension of the sum of those direction spaces, again
greater than q. This identity follows by summing their relative-open
subsets; translation of their affine hulls does not affect it. In both
cases the intermediate section has infinite H_q, exceeding the finite
threshold.

Otherwise the endpoint sections lie in parallel q-planes. Translation
to their common direction space is isometric and ordinary q-dimensional
Brunn--Minkowski applies to their measurable convex sections, including
nonclosed ones. Its root lower bound, the strict endpoint inequalities,
and convexity of ell give the displayed strict superlevel inequality.
There is no use of q-dimensional Brunn--Minkowski on nonparallel
q-planes and no zero-extension concavity assumption. Real-base sections
of infinite H_q are retained. No measurability or continuity of the
real-base superlevel function is needed; only convexity of its sets is
used. In particular a finite convex ell may have boundary
discontinuities without invalidating the proof.

## 2. Nonclosed parity Helly and the selected original caps

The positive base set is midpoint-closed for same-parity pairs. The
Minkowski midpoint contains a q-dimensional body; its integer fiber
cannot have dimension greater than q by definition of q. Thus its base
is again positive. This argument does not assume all positive fiber
direction spaces are equal.

The finite midpoint/parity Helly proof for affine inequalities and
polytopes is valid: the threshold exclusion set is compact, a maximum
of the sum of thresholds is attained, each nonsaturated threshold has
its own strict contact witness, and same-parity witnesses would have
an excluded-system solution at their midpoint. At most k original
inequalities therefore suffice.

For clarity, its extension to arbitrary, possibly nonclosed, convex
sets E is the following exact finite-trace argument. Replace E by
`conv(E intersect P)`. This is a possibly empty polytope contained in E,
and it has exactly the same trace on P as E. Apply the polytope theorem,
then transfer the traces back. This proof is also written in Section 3
of `candidate 05b459fea3722ebb`;
the weighted-center source supplies the inequality/polytope part and
the general midpoint-label extension.

The local residual premise says each positive base misses at least one
of the finitely many superlevels. Helly selects at most k superlevels
whose intersection misses P. The union of their original index sets
has at most kt indices. At every base at least one selected residual
set has measure at most the prescribed threshold; the residual from
the union of all selected caps is a subset of that residual set.
This proves the stronger pointwise assertion before summation. Empty
index sets, vertical caps, whole-fiber boundary mass, and cuts whose
continuous restriction vanishes do not require changing the argument.

## 3. Constants and finite optimization

Finite subadditivity of the selected union gives exactly
`kt B >= M-sum ell(z)^q`; no cap multipliers or artificial cap masses
are used. Under `sum ell(z)^q <= (1-tg)M`, with `0<=tg<=1`, this is
`B>=gM/k`. The planar pair threshold is exactly M/9 because
`1-2 gamma_2=1/9`. The occupied-parity count is k, independently of
the number of superlevels selected by Helly.

The affine-majorant program is attained in its finite-dimensional
closed space of evaluation vectors: positive lower constraints and
bounded objective sublevels bound each coordinate. Its lower bound
one, constant-majorant upper bound, and equality for affine volume
roots follow directly. Strict convexity for q>1 gives uniqueness of
the minimizing evaluation vector as stated.

For the sharper hinge program the actual sampled residual minimum is
attained over finitely many index sets. Its zero values correctly
impose no lower bound on the affine L. The epigraph constraints in
`(L,T)` are finitely many non-strict linear inequalities. Eliminating
the affine coefficients projects this polyhedron to a closed
polyhedron in the T variables. Nonnegative bounded objective sublevels
are compact, including q=1, so an optimum T is attained and has an
associated L. Replacing T by the positive part of that L preserves
feasibility and cannot increase the objective. Thus the original hinge
program itself is attained; escaping affine coefficients cause no
gap. The all-zero residual case is attained by L=0.

## 4. Counting and scope

For q=0, every nonempty integer fiber is a singleton. The separate
argument uses projections of the actual convex residual sets, not a
zero-th root, and recovers the exact local-to-global cover theorem.
Any covering cap family has a one-cap local cover at each singleton,
so at most k original caps cover S and the counting budget is M/k.

The statement makes no normalization of the integer lattice, does not
discard lower-dimensional fibers carrying the chosen intrinsic
measure, and includes all oblique ambient halfspaces. Its applications
to the three-cap small-minimum alternative correctly retain the
every-fiber premise and the optimized residual-cost condition.
Neither is claimed automatically at a mixed-integer extremizer.

No substantive correction was found. The author has added the short
nonclosed finite-trace Helly step directly to Section 3 in response to
the audit, so the source now supplies this scope extension explicitly.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
